podcast.title: Consistent Instrumentalist - Defines Fleetwood Mac's Sound
podcast.body: John McVie, as the bassist, along with drummer Mick Fleetwood, were the only instrumentalists who remained consistent throughout Fleetwood Mac's existence, largely shaping the band's sound. His bass lines, alongside Fleetwood's drums, provided the foundation for various iterations of the band, from early tracks like "Rattlesnake Shake" with Peter Green to later hits like "Tusk" with Lindsey Buckingham. "But the only instrumentalists who have remained consistent and who are still the band's namesake are drummer Fleetwood and bassist Mick Vee."

podcast.title: Namesake of Fleetwood Mac - Rhythm Section
podcast.body: John McVie, a bassist, along with drummer Mick Fleetwood, became the namesake of the band Fleetwood Mac, which was formed by former members of John Mayall's Bluesbreakers. This naming convention highlighted the enduring presence of the rhythm section, even as lead guitarists changed frequently throughout the band's history. "But it was named after its rhythm section, a drummer named Mick Fleetwood and a bassist named John Mac McVee."

podcast.title: Target of "Don't Stop"
podcast.body: John McVie, bassist for Fleetwood Mac, was the target of the "genial diss record" "Don't Stop," written by his ex-wife and bandmate, Christine McVie, for the "Rumours" album. "Even the seemingly sunny Rumors single Don't Stop, written by keyboardist Christine McVe was a genial diss record against her ex-husband, bassist John McVe."
